papers.title: Lipid homeostasis and cellular metabolism in neurodegenerative diseases: A maturing framework to guide therapeutic development.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and dementia with Lewy bodies have long been viewed through the lens of protein aggregation. Emerging evidence, however, highlights lipid transfer, load, metabolism, and cellular homeostasis as upstream drivers of pathology. This perspective integrates established neurobiological, genetic, and mechanistic evidence of lipid dysfunction and outlines how these pathways can guide patient stratification, biomarker discovery, and therapeutic development. Of critical importance, lipid transport and lysosomal and trafficking networks are at the center of cholesterol regulation, glycosphingolipid clearance, endolysosomal function, and neuron-glia lipid exchange across genetic and sporadic neurodegenerative diseases. We present an integrated framework where correcting lipid imbalances and metabolic dysregulation may complement or obviate protein-targeted approaches, creating more precise clinical trials and combination strategies. By re-centering the therapeutic focus on lipid and cellular metabolism, we aim to catalyze translational advances in neurodegenerative disease treatment.

papers.title: Serum Insulin-Like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1) in Parkinson's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a common neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive motor and non-motor symptoms. Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1), a neuroprotective hormone, has been proposed as a potential biomarker in PD. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate differences in serum IGF-1 levels between people with PD (PwPD) and healthy controls, and to assess associations with symptom severity. METHODS: We conducted a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science on December 7, 2024. Observational studies comparing serum IGF-1 in PwPD and healthy controls, or assessing its associations with PD symptoms, were included. Study quality was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. A random-effects meta-analysis pooled mean differences (MD) in IGF-1 levels, and correlation coefficients were synthesized for motor symptoms. Non-motor symptom associations were analyzed using effect direction plots. RESULTS: Eighteen studies with 2,480 participants (1,465 PwPD; 1,015 controls) were included. PwPD had significantly higher serum IGF-1 levels than controls (MD: 21.3 ng/mL; 95CI: 11.49, 31.12; p < 0.001). Elevated IGF-1 was consistent across early/late-stage and drug-naïve/treated PwPD, with no significant subgroup differences. Meta-analysis of five studies (413 PwPD) showed an inverse correlation between IGF-1 levels and motor symptom severity (r = -0.35; 95% CI: -0.53, -0.08; p < 0.01), although individual study findings were heterogeneous, and the certainty of evidence was low. Non-motor symptoms also showed no consistent associations. CONCLUSIONS: PwPD exhibit elevated serum IGF-1 levels and may be inversely associated with motor symptom severity. IGF-1's relationship with non-motor symptoms remains unclear and requires further study. Longitudinal research is needed to determine IGF-1's utility as a PD biomarker.

papers.title: Diffuse mild TBI reveals spatially selective vulnerability from early olfactory disruption to delayed substantia nigra involvement.
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is associated with an increased risk of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet the anatomical routes through which diffuse injury confers selective neuronal vulnerability remain poorly defined. The olfactory system occupies a critical peripheral-central interface: primary olfactory neurons project unmyelinated axons through the cribriform plate into the olfactory bulb, rendering this pathway susceptible to mechanical stress while overlapping with one of the earliest sites of α-synuclein pathology in PD. Here, we tested whether diffuse mild TBI produces spatially and temporally distinct neuropathological responses across the olfactory-nigrostriatal axis. Adult C57BL/6 mice underwent mild TBI using the Closed Head Impact Model of Rotational Acceleration and were assessed at 24 h, 1 month, and 6 months post-injury. Holocranioimmunohistochemistry preserving anatomical continuity between the olfactory epithelium (OE) and olfactory bulb enabled integrated analysis of peripheral and central structures. Diffuse injury produced acute axonal disruption of olfactory receptor neurons and was accompanied by transient immune cell accumulation and altered neuronal turnover in the OE. These changes largely resolved by one month, although a modest reduction in mature receptor neurons persisted. In contrast, central olfactory regions demonstrated sustained microglial elevation together with delayed increases in phosphorylated α-synuclein occurring without corresponding changes in total α-synuclein expression. Delayed vulnerability emerged within the substantia nigra, where dopaminergic neuron density was reduced at six months despite preserved striatal terminals. This was accompanied by increased total α-synuclein in the absence of phosphorylation at serine-129, consistent with altered protein handling rather than phosphorylation-dominant aggregation. papers.title: Early and Extensive Degeneration of Sensory Neurons in Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postmortem studies have shown significant degeneration of the peripheral nervous system (PNS) in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3). Although PNS involvement accelerates overall ataxia progression, PNS biomarkers for therapeutic trials are lacking and our mechanistic understanding of related clinical manifestations remains incomplete. OBJECTIVE: We employed a multimodal approach to characterize and quantify peripheral sensory nervous system degeneration throughout the course of SCA3. METHODS: Forty SCA3 mutation carriers, including 10 preataxic individuals, were enrolled in this study. Detailed clinical assessments of ataxia and neuropathy severity were combined with high-resolution nerve ultrasound and electrophysiological examinations to evaluate cross-sectional areas (CSAs) and sensory action potential amplitudes of upper and lower limb nerves. RESULTS: Sensory axonal loss in at least one nerve was found in 97% of ataxic and 50% of preataxic individuals. Ultrasound examinations showed CSA reductions at one or more measurement sites in at least two nerves in all participants. Upper limb nerves were more commonly affected than the sural nerve, which supports a widespread, non-length-dependent pattern of axonal damage. The degree of sensory axonal loss was associated with ataxia severity, estimated disease duration, and patient-reported ability to perform activities of daily living. CONCLUSIONS: Abnormalities of the peripheral sensory nervous system are highly prevalent in SCA3, emerge before ataxia onset, and reflect disease severity. The combination of electrophysiological and ultrasound profiles suggests early involvement of the dorsal root ganglia, highlighting an underestimated source of (sensory) ataxia in SCA3. Longitudinal studies are warranted to validate the biomarker potential of these measures. © 2026 The Author(s). papers.title: Brain-heart coupling in Parkinson's disease: from autonomic dysfunction to network physiology.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular autonomic dysfunction is a well-established feature of Parkinson's disease (PD), yet the brain and cardiovascular system are still largely investigated as separate physiological domains. This separation may overlook an important dimension of PD pathophysiology: the dynamic communication between them. Here, we examine emerging evidence that brain-heart coupling itself is altered in PD. A focused PubMed search identified studies directly relating neural activity to cardiac dynamics, complemented by relevant physiological and autonomic literature. Despite a small and heterogeneous evidence base, electrophysiological, neuroimaging, and dynamic network studies suggest disrupted central-cardiac coordination. Alterations are detectable in early and de novo

papers.title: Lewy pathology accumulates in enlarged corticostriatal synapses in α-synucleinopathies.
papers.abstract: Lewy body diseases, including Parkinson's disease, Parkinson's disease dementia and dementia with Lewy bodies, are neurodegenerative disorders characterized by the accumulation of misfolded α-synuclein in the form of Lewy pathology. A hallmark of these diseases is degeneration of the nigrostriatal pathway, resulting in loss of dopaminergic input to the striatum and consequent motor dysfunction. Lewy pathology is present in many regions outside the substantia nigra, and cortical Lewy pathology is the best correlate of cognitive decline in individuals who develop dementia. In addition, there is a high burden of neuritic Lewy pathology in the putamen, though the neuronal origin of this pathology is unclear. In the current study, we quantified the burden of Lewy pathology in the putamen across the spectrum of Lewy body diseases. Immunohistochemistry was used to quantify the Lewy burden in the putamen, cingulate and frontal cortices of 8 controls and 28 Lewy body disease cases. Even in Parkinson's disease cases without dementia, we observed a nearly complete striatal dopaminergic denervation among Lewy body disease cases. Consistent with this denervation, most α-synuclein pathology did not colocalize with dopaminergic terminals, but was instead enriched in excitatory terminals. This enrichment in glutamatergic terminals was associated with swollen axons, but not with overall loss of those terminals. These findings suggest that Lewy pathology accumulates at excitatory corticostriatal synapses prior to overt synaptic degeneration and could contribute to cognitive decline in Lewy body diseases.

papers.title: Comprehensive benchmarking of EEG biomarkers for Parkinson's disease: robustness, reliability, and clinical discriminability across multiple datasets.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a high-temporal-resolution, noninvasive window into some of the abnormalities underlying Parkinson's disease (PD), yet reported electrophysiological biomarkers vary widely across studies due to differences in preprocessing, feature extraction, and analytical pipelines. Here we provide the first comprehensive, multi-dataset benchmarking of 16 EEG-derived biomarkers, including phase-amplitude coupling, beta burst metrics, aperiodic components, complexity measures, and beta waveform features, to evaluate their robustness, reliability, and clinical discriminability. Using three independent resting-state EEG datasets, with two preprocessing conditions evaluated for one dataset, we assessed the effects of preprocessing, window length, within-session variability, channel aggregation strategies, and clinical group differences (healthy controls vs. PD OFF-medication, healthy controls vs. PD ON-medication, and PD OFF- vs. ON-medication). Cross-dataset reproducibility of group-level effects was additionally evaluated using effect-size pattern similarity, biomarker rank concordance, effect-direction consistency, and random-effects meta-analysis. Aperiodic features, entropy and complexity measures, and fractal metrics demonstrated high methodological robustness across preprocessing methods, window lengths, and aggregation strategies, and several showed disease- and medication-related effects across datasets, although effect magnitude and statistical significance varied across datasets and analytical conditions. In contrast, oscillatory biomarkers, including beta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, burst-derived metrics, and waveform-asymmetry features, showed substantial variability across methodological choices and lower within-session consistency. papers.title: Strategies to establish a biologically defined Parkinson's disease cohort prior to the onset of clinically significant motor symptoms.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.abstract: Identifying individuals at risk for neurodegeneration is a priority for clinical trials. Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI) deploys strategies to enroll individuals before typical clinical Parkinson's disease symptoms: recruiting polysomnogram-confirmed REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) and central identification of hyposmia via smell testing. Groups were divided into RBD with and without hyposmia (RBD+Hyposmia, RBD-Hyposmia) and hyposmia with and without self-reported dream enactment behavior (Hyposmia+DEB, Hyposmia-DEB). Participants underwent clinical and biomarker testing including CSF alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay (CSFaSynSAA) and dopamine transporter imaging. While all enrollment strategies showed robust enrichment for CSFaSynSAA positivity, RBD+Hyposmia and Hyposmia+DEB were more likely CSFaSynSAA+ (94% and 85%) vs RBD-Hyposmia (40%) and Hyposmia-DEB (55%). Among CSFaSynSAA+, RBD+Hyposmia and Hyposmia+DEB had more mood, autonomic, and cognitive symptoms than Hyposmia-DEB. PPMI identified a large biologically-defined early neuronal synucleinopathy cohort and demonstrated biomarker and multi-domain clinical heterogeneity within CSFaSynSAA+ individuals prior to symptom onset.

papers.title: Health consequences of paraquat exposure, a review.
papers.abstract: Paraquat (PQ) is a widely used herbicide with high toxicity to humans and animals. Exposure to PQ occurs through inhalation, ingestion, or dermal contact and can result in severe systemic poisoning. This narrative review synthesizes experimental and clinical evidence from 165 studies identified through searches of Web of Science, PubMed, and Scopus covering publications from January 1989 through February 2026. The review examines PQ-induced toxicity across multiple organ systems, including the lungs, kidneys, liver, heart, nervous system, gastrointestinal tract, and reproductive and endocrine systems. PQ exposure is associated with oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, immune dysregulation, and cellular death, contributing to diverse organ-specific injuries. Experimental studies have also investigated potential links between PQ exposure and neurodegenerative processes, including those relevant to Parkinson's disease; however, epidemiological evidence remains heterogeneous. Current treatment options for PQ poisoning remain limited, underscoring the importance of prevention and exposure reduction. The principal contribution of this review is an integrated mechanistic framework linking oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, immune dysregulation, and apoptosis to multi-organ toxicity. This framework highlights shared biological pathways across organ systems while identifying important gaps in translating experimental findings into clinical practice. Further research should prioritize improved exposure assessment, validation of relevant biomarkers, and rigorous evaluation of protective strategies and therapeutic interventions.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-based voice biomarkers for early detection and monitoring of neurological diseases: current evidence, limitations, and clinical perspectives.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring of neurological diseases remain major clinical challenges because current diagnostic approaches are often expensive, invasive, or insufficiently sensitive to detect early functional changes. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach for analyzing voice and speech as non-invasive digital biomarkers capable of capturing subtle alterations associated with neurological dysfunction. METHODS: This narrative review analyzed studies published between 2015 and 2026 retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. The review critically examines the limitations of current neurological diagnostic methods, summarizes the available evidence on AI-based voice and speech biomarkers, discusses machine learning and deep learning approaches applied to speech analysis, and evaluates the methodological, ethical, and regulatory challenges that currently limit their clinical implementation. RESULTS: Current evidence indicates that AI-based voice biomarkers have considerable potential for screening, diagnostic support, and longitudinal monitoring of neurological disorders, including Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, and other neurodegenerative conditions. Several studies report high diagnostic performance under controlled experimental settings. However, substantial heterogeneity in study design, sample size, languages, speech acquisition protocols, validation strategies, and reporting standards limits direct comparison between studies and hinders clinical translation. External validation and prospective multicenter studies remain scarce. CONCLUSION: AI-based voice analysis represents a promising, scalable, and non-invasive complement to conventional neurological assessment, with particular potential for remote screening and disease monitoring. Nevertheless, current evidence does not yet support routine clinical implementation. Future progress will de

papers.title: Network Localization of Anxiety as an Early Manifestation of Alzheimer's Disease-related Neurodegeneration.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Anxiety is a prominent neuropsychiatric symptom in preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the neural circuitry linking anxiety and AD remains uncharacterized. We assessed whether anxiety in preclinical AD is independently associated with AD-related neurodegeneration and localizes to a common anxiety network. METHODS: In cognitively unimpaired (CU) older adults with 3T MRI and amyloid-β PET (N=1,775), we examined whether an established AD-related atrophy network is associated with anxiety (STAI-6). Then, using Atrophy Network Mapping (ANM), which maps individual cortical atrophy patterns onto a normative functional connectome (N=1000), we derived an anxiety network. We tested its 1) spatial convergence with the AD network and with a causal anxiety network derived from lesion and neuromodulation data, 2) specificity relative to depression, 3) generalizability in samples from independent cohorts with AD and Parkinson's disease (total n=878), and 4) association with longitudinal outcomes. RESULTS: In CU older adults, greater AD-network atrophy was associated with higher anxiety, independent of depression, cognition, cortical atrophy, and amyloid burden. Anxiety localized to a network closely resembling the AD network (r=0.74, p=0.04) and the causal anxiety network (r=0.72, p=0.02). This convergence extended across the AD continuum and to the Parkinson's disease cohort and was specific to anxiety relative to depression. Greater anxiety-network atrophy was associated with cognitive decline over 4.6 years. CONCLUSION: Anxiety localizes to a brain circuit resembling the AD-related atrophy network, is consistent across the AD continuum and may extend beyond AD. These findings support anxiety as an independent marker of early AD-related neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Sleep components, depressive subdomains and quality of life in Parkinson's disease: A cross-sectional exploratory analysis.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Sleep disturbances and depressive symptoms are prevalent non-motor burdens in Parkinson's disease (PD) and are closely associated with poorer health-related quality of life (QoL). Non-motor symptoms of PD exhibit substantial heterogeneity. It remains unclear whether distinct sleep disturbances show differential correlations with physical and mental QoL, and whether specific depressive subdimensions are implicated in these relationships. This exploratory study analyzed direct and indirect associations among sleep components, depressive subdimensions, and physical-mental QoL in hospitalized patients with PD. METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed data from 55 hospitalized patients with idiopathic PD who completed the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), the 24-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAMD), the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), and the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36). Spearman correlation and multivariable regression analyses were performed to assess bivariate associations and independent correlates of QoL. Exploratory PROCESS analyses were further implemented as hypothesis-generating secondary analyses to examine symptom-level indirect associations; all findings were interpreted as cross-sectional and non-causal. RESULTS: Spearman correlation analyses showed that the PSQI total score was significantly correlated with both PCS and MCS (both p CONCLUSION: Within this hospitalized PD cohort, depressive symptoms represented the dominant correlate of QoL. Specific sleep components exhibited indirect association patterns with QoL through distinct depressive subdimensions. These preliminary findings underline the heterogeneity of PD non-motor symptoms and provide a hypothesis-generating framework for future longitudinal validation and targeted intervention studies.

papers.title: Trends and future projections of Parkinson's disease burden in China: findings from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a major public health burden in China. We aimed to analyze temporal trends in PD burden across China from 1990 to 2023, and project the future burden through 2050. METHODS: Using data from the 2023 Global Burden of Disease (GBD 2023) database, prevalence, incidence, deaths, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years of life lost (YLLs), and years lived with disability (YLDs) of PD in 31 provinces, autonomous regions, municipalities, and the two special administrative regions (SAR) of Hong Kong and Macao of China from 1990 to 2023 were analyzed. Age-standardized rates (ASRs) and the average annual percent change (AAPCs) were calculated. Changes in case numbers were decomposed using a Das Gupta framework, and future burden to 2050 was projected using a probabilistic model-averaging approach. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2023, the age-standardized prevalence, incidence, and YLD rates of PD increased in China, whereas the age-standardized mortality, YLL, and DALY rates decreased. The number of people living with PD increased from 781.29 thousand (95% UI 629.39-973.58) in 1990 to 3445.69 thousand (95% UI 2804.28-4243.67) in 2023, and incident cases increased from 99.51 thousand (95% UI 82.51-118.00) in 1990 to 379.69 thousand (95% UI 319.28-447.58) in 2023. The age-standardized prevalence rate increased from 106.56 per 100,000 (95% UI 86.16-131.29) to 148.74 per 100,000 (95% UI 122.07-183.52) (AAPC=1.03%, 95% CI 0.98-1.09), whereas the age-standardized mortality, DALY, and YLL rates decreased from 4.69 per 100,000 to 3.78 per 100,000, 92.40 per 100,000 to 77.87 per 100,000, and 77.37 per 100,000 to 56.81 per 100,000, respectively. The age-standardized YLD rate increased from 15.03 per 100,000 to 21.07 per 100,000. papers.title: Small-fiber degeneration, sensory dysfunction, and nociception comorbidity in central neurodegenerative disease.
papers.abstract: Progressive neurodegenerative disease typically calls for clinical effort to improve cognitive and motor deficits. It is also focused on improving patients' quality of life. However, across these dementias and other diseases, the underlying causes and potential mechanisms remain unclear. Most experimental and clinical research focuses on the central nervous system, examining pathogenic proteins such as tau and amyloid beta, as well as the potential cascade following mitochondrial damage and neuroinflammation. Although peripheral involvement, including gut microbiome influences and other visceral organs, is well-documented, the peripheral nervous system remains an understudied component of these progressive diseases. As peripheral terminals of primary afferent neurons are exposed to inflammatory or toxic mediators, these neurons respond to these threats via neuron-specific phenotypic changes, including the generation of pain. Although normal peripheral sensitization is protective, exposure to damage in a chronic disease state can have long-term detrimental effects. Diseases that lead to central neurodegeneration often also feature peripheral neuropathy and chronic pain. We provide an overview of the incidence of peripheral neuropathy within these diseases, the contribution of changes in sensation to disease, and secondary neuropathic phenotypes resulting from disease. Woven in are discussions of the intersection of degeneration and toxic protein aggregation, briefly touching on resulting inflammatory signaling. Altogether, this review aims to synthesize current understanding of sensory peripheral nerve involvement across these neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: A Local Enrichment Computational Framework to Identify Disease-Enriched Physical Activity Patterns.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.abstract: Wearable accelerometers enable continuous monitoring of physical activity (PA), yet conventional summary measures and population-wide clustering approaches may overlook disease-associated behavioral heterogeneity. Here we introduce LocPA, a computational framework that identifies disease-enriched PA patterns through confounder-adjusted activity profiling, similarity network construction, local disease-enrichment testing and community detection. Applying LocPA to 24-hour accelerometry profiles from the UK Biobank, we identified two recurring PA phenotypes across six diseases spanning cardiometabolic, neurological, psychiatric, renal and cardiovascular conditions: a low-activity phenotype characterized by reduced daytime activity and a sleep-disrupted phenotype characterized by reduced daytime and elevated nocturnal activity. In hypertension and diabetes, the sleep-disrupted phenotype was associated with greater disease burden and less favorable clinical and metabolic profiles, differences not consistently captured by conventional PA summary measures. LocPA also identified disease-specific temporal patterns, particularly in Parkinsons disease. Analyses in an independent National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey cohort supported the recurrence of hypertension- and diabetes-enriched patterns across populations and accelerometry measurements. LocPA provides a flexible, disease-driven approach for uncovering clinically relevant temporal PA patterns, with potential applications in disease risk characterization and personalized behavioral interventions.

papers.title: Mediterranean-ketogenic vs. medium-chain triglyceride supplemented Mediterranean diet: Effects on the gut-brain-immune axis in Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Ketogenic diets have been proposed as potential neuroprotective interventions for Parkinson's disease (PD), but concerns remain regarding their effects on the gut microbiome and gut-brain-immune axis. We conducted a randomized crossover trial comparing 8-week Mediterranean-ketogenic (MeDi-KD) versus medium-chain triglyceride-supplemented Mediterranean (MeDi-MCT) diets, separated by an 8-week washout (NCT05469997). Primary outcomes included changes in gut microbiome taxonomic and functional profiles, fecal short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production, and biomarkers of intestinal permeability and inflammation. Neither intervention significantly altered microbiome diversity or functional gene abundance, established features of PD-associated dysbiosis, nor fecal or plasma biomarkers of intestinal permeability (zonulin) or inflammation (calprotectin). The MeDi-KD modestly reduced total fecal SCFAs, while both interventions increased the relative abundance of Roseburia hominis

papers.title: Reliability and construct validity of the Italian EQ-5D-5 L in Parkinson's disease: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) substantially affects health-related quality of life (HRQoL). The EQ-5D-5 L is a preference-based patient-reported outcome measure that supports cross-condition comparison and health-economic evaluation, but its measurement properties have not been established in people with PD in Italy. This study evaluated short-term reproducibility and construct validity through a priori hypothesis testing; score distributions and inter-dimensional associations were also described. METHODS: This cross-sectional psychometric study included a 48-hour retest component. Participants completed the EQ-5D-5 L, the Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire-39 (PDQ-39), and the 12-item Short Form Health Survey (SF-12). Short-term reproducibility was assessed using quadratic-weighted Cohen's kappa and exact agreement for the five dimensions and single-measures, two-way random-effects, absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficients for the EQ-Index and EQ-VAS. Construct validity was examined using prespecified directional and magnitude hypotheses tested with Spearman correlations; Pearson correlations were used as sensitivity analyses. Post hoc analyses examined routine-care clinical measures and ordered motor-severity categories. RESULTS: Eighty participants completed the questionnaires, and 60 underwent retesting. Fifty-nine distinct health states were observed, with one participant reporting full health. Agreement was high for the EQ-Index (ICC = 0.901, 95% CI 0.840-0.940) and EQ-VAS (ICC = 0.938, 95% CI 0.899-0.963), whereas dimension-level kappa ranged from 0.632 to 0.916. All 20 directional hypotheses were confirmed, but only 6 of the 16 prespecified magnitude criteria were met. papers.title: Occupational pesticide exposure and risk of Parkinson's disease: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT: Parkinson’s disease is a rapidly increasing neurological disorder in terms of global prevalence and is associated with disability and reduced quality of life. Occupational exposure to pesticides has long been considered a potential risk factor, but there is a lack of a systematic review attempting to derive the exposure–response relationship. This protocol outlines the planned methodology for a systematic review and where feasible, meta-analysis to evaluate the relationship between occupational pesticide exposure and Parkinson’s disease. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: We will include epidemiological studies (cohort, case–control and cross-sectional studies) examining the relationship between occupational pesticide exposure and Parkinson’s disease in adults of working age or older. Exposure may be assessed via self-report, expert assessment, job exposure matrices, direct observation or technical measurements. Eligible outcomes are clinically confirmed Parkinson’s disease. The literature search will be conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, NIOSHTIC-2 and ArbLINE, supplemented by grey literature. Two reviewers will independently screen studies, extract data and assess risk of bias. Where feasible, effect estimates will be pooled using random-effects meta-analysis and explored through sensitivity analyses. We will evaluate the certainty of evidence using the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: As this review is based solely on published data, ethical approval is not necessary. Results will be disseminated through a peer-reviewed publication and relevant scientific meetings. PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD1089055.

papers.title: Changes in Clinical Outcomes and Peripheral Cytokines during Duloxetine Add-on Therapy in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neuroinflammation is implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD), and antidepressants may have anti-inflammatory and motor benefits. The effects of duloxetine on inflammatory biomarkers and clinical outcomes in PD remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: To assess changes in motor symptoms, quality of life, and serum cytokines during add-on duloxetine treatment in PD. METHODS: Seventeen patients with PD without other chronic inflammatory diseases received add-on duloxetine for 8 weeks in an open-label, uncontrolled trial. Clinical outcomes included Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (UPDRS), modified Hoehn and Yahr (HY), and Parkinson's Disease Questionnaire-39 (PDQ-39) scores. Serum TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-10 levels were measured at baseline and follow-up. RESULTS: UPDRS, activities of daily living, and PDQ-39 scores decreased during treatment. Ten patients achieved ≥5-point UPDRS reductions. TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 decreased, whereas IL-10 increased after treatment. CONCLUSIONS: Add-on duloxetine was associated with changes in clinical outcomes and inflammatory markers in patients with PD.

papers.title: Compound heterozygous and digenic inheritance in early-onset Parkinson's disease: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Compound heterozygous (CH) genotypes represent an established biallelic autosomal-recessive mechanism in early-onset Parkinson's disease (EOPD), whereas digenic inheritance (DI) has been proposed for variant combinations across two genes but is more difficult to establish. We systematically evaluated the genetic architecture and clinical features of CH cases and cases reported as DI in the published literature. METHODS: This PRISMA-compliant systematic review included studies reporting CH or DI EOPD through September 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and curated variant- and case-level information. Variants were harmonized using current Human Genome Variation Society nomenclature and classified by gene, variant type, ancestry, and inheritance model. RESULTS: We included 106 studies comprising 304 CH and 16 DI cases.
